header.name: Logic and Artificial Intelligence
header.description: It is well known that the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has roots in logic (philosophical and mathematical). In fact, many of the most influential figures in AI’s early days had planned to use ideas from philosophical logic to formalize commonsense reasoning or reasoning by a rational agent. In turn, applications in AI has led to numerous fascinating new logical systems. The goal of this course is to study the logical frameworks that can be used to model reasoning by and about rational agents. This would require us to consider many different aspects, such as, action, knowledge, belief, and revision. The course will attempt to cover formal approaches to these with the goal of formalizing systems where these things work together. What this course is: This is a course on formal logic. The material is theoretical. What this course is not: This is not a computer science or course or a course in AI. There are no algorithms discussed or coding involved.
prerequisites_desirable: A course in logic such as IML (MTH300/500) could be helpful.
prerequisites_desirable_resolved: A course in logic such as IML (MTH300/500) could be helpful.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to determine the roots of the thriving field of AI in philosophical and mathematical logic.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to apply the techniques of modal logic and belief revision in the context of rational agents.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to describe the complex phenomena that arise when rational agents interact and construct formal models for these.
